extracted.intended_audience: Congress, federal policymakers, and administrators of national scholarship/fellowship programs (education and research institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Design and administration guidance for a federal program (the proposed National Science Reserve) to discover and develop scientific talent, covering scale, eligibility, selection procedures, support levels, state allocation, administrative bodies, and service obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit-only selection (no discrimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who receive benefits under the plan should be selected solely on the basis of merit, without regard to sex, race, color, or creed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection must be on merit alone. This is stated as a firm principle for awarding National Science Reserve Scholarships and Fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial need should not be a factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The question whether or not financial need should be considered as a factor in awarding benefits under the plan ... We conclude that need should not be a factor in the awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons given: means test of parents would be difficult or impossible to administer equitably; recipients would be labeled as poor; unsympathetic parents might block benefits. Implement the program without a means-test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection based on tests of ability and aptitude
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards of Science Reserve Scholarships for college training for the bachelor's degree should be based upon tests of ability and aptitude to ensure that the successful candidates will be oriented to scientific and technological pursuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests should be prepared by a central/national staff in accordance with best thought and given to all applicants nationwide. Tests are intended to ensure orientation toward scientific/technological work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum national standard for certification
rubrics_metrics.description: It being provided, however, that no applicants shall be certified who do not attain a certain minimum national standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The national organization will apply a national cutoff; only applicants meeting this minimum may be certified for consideration by State committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage certification and state final selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The national staff ... would certify to the State Committees a number of qualified candidates equal to twice the State's quota ... The dossiers of these candidates would be sent to the State committees and those committees would have the responsibility of making the final selections of the Scholars up to the number of the State's quota.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National organization evaluates tests and other data and supplies a certified pool (twice quota); State committees perform final selections from that pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: State quota allocation by secondary-school graduates
rubrics_metrics.description: The 6,000 proposed scholarships should be assigned to the States on the basis of the number of their secondary school graduates of the previous year as related to the national total of such graduates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the basis of 1939-40 figures; allocation formula includes public high school graduates plus one-sixth of private and parochial secondary school enrollment. Territories and insular possessions to be included (would reduce State quotas).

rubrics_metrics.name: State selection committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees of selection would be set up in each State. These committees ... should consist of five members, to wit: three scientists, one of whom should serve as chairman; one member of a college or university faculty, trained and experienced in the field of selection and guidance; and one representative of secondary education within the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one of the scientists should be from agriculture or from industry within the State. These committees receive dossiers and make final selections up to the State quota.

rubrics_metrics.name: National administrative agency and advisory bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be our recommendation that the foundation, or any similar organization which may be established, should make arrangements for choosing Scholars and Fellows under the proposed plan through the National Academy of Sciences ... the operation of the plan ... should be entrusted to the Academy's operating agency, the National Research Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A central administrative staff chosen for ability and integrity should be set up; advisory bodies expert in selection and guidance must be established to ensure up-to-date and fair methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale of undergraduate support (GI Bill parity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scale of support for the undergraduate students selected under the proposed plan should be that provided by Congress under the so-called GI Bill of Rights, namely, tuition and other fees up to $500 annually and, for personal support, $50 a month during the months of each year when the scholars actually are engaged in full-time study. Benefits ... if married, should receive ... $75 monthly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial support package is explicitly recommended to match GI Bill levels: up to $500/year tuition/fees, $50/month individual support, $75/month if married.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility includes those who worked in business/industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits under the plan should not be restricted to young and recent secondary school graduates but should be available also to those who, having worked in business and industry, desire to obtain scientific training at the college level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program should allow entrants who are returning to study after industry/business experience; not limited to immediate secondary-school-to-college pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment in National Science Reserve and service obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient ... shall agree that, upon the completion of his undergraduate or graduate training, he shall be enrolled in the National Science Reserve and be liable to call into the service of the Federal Government, in connection with scientific or technical work in time of war or of a national emergency declared by Congress or proclaimed by the President ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation is a quid pro quo: enrollment in Reserve, liability for call to service in war/national emergency (call at Government option), conditions and salary to be determined by President; Congress to determine exact extent/duration. Additionally, members pledge peacetime advisory/consulting assistance insofar as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' professional intention (not absolute obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of the Scholarships and Fellowships should be understood by the recipients as indicating intention to engage professionally in scientific and technological work but not as constituting an absolute obligation to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarship acceptance signals intended career orientation toward science/technology but does not legally bind recipients to a lifelong professional requirement (apart from Reserve call if enacted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational institutions' obligation to provide commensurate training
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the central purpose of the plan—to provide scientific training for students of superior ability and equal opportunity to all American youth to qualify in competition for such training—educational institutions will face the obligation of providing a training commensurate intellectually with the superior ability of this special group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must offer programs appropriate to highly selected students; standard rank-and-file programs are not suitable for these scholars/fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scale targets and caution on numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: We propose that the number of undergraduate students of science and technology assisted under the plan shall be 6,000 annually and that the number of assisted doctoral students in the same fields shall be 250 or 300 annually ... Maximum annual costs ... may reach, after the fourth year of operation, $29,000,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These figures are executive judgments (not provable); they are intended as reasonable starting points and should not be frozen—should be changed in the light of experience and future demand studies. Maximum totals (e.g., 24,000 undergraduates in 4-year max) are given for planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for graduate-duration flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: These highly selected students, if they proceed to doctorates, in many cases will be able to obtain that degree after 6 years of undergraduate and graduate work; but provision should be made for those who require 3, instead of 2, years of graduate work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow variation in graduate training duration (2–3 years) when planning fellowship length and budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized testing procedures and dossier collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative staff of the national over-all organization, in cooperation with the advisory bodies, would prepare tests ... These tests would be given to all applicants throughout the country and the test reports would be sent to the national organization for evaluation. The national staff also would collect other relevant data and judgments concerning each applicant ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement centralized test preparation and national aggregation of scores and supplemental materials (dossiers) to support fair, comparable evaluation across states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dossiers transmitted to State committees
rubrics_metrics.description: The dossiers of these candidates would be sent to the State committees ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After national evaluation and certification, full candidate dossiers must be supplied to state selection committees for local final decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: national program with local administration
rubrics_metrics.description: It is agreed by the Committee ... that while the plan must be national in character, the principle of local administration must be recognized. The American scene ... has infinite variety and intense individuality at close range. This must be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the administrative framework to be national in standards and scale, but delegate selection/implementation nuances to local/state bodies to respect regional diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating an 'elect'; use broad base and successive selection
rubrics_metrics.description: To get top leadership there must be a relatively large base of high ability selected for development and then successive skimmings of the cream of ability at successive times and at higher levels. No one can select from the bottom those who will be the leaders at the top ... We think it very important that every boy and girl shall know that, if he shows that he 'has what it takes,' the sky is the limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program design should favor broad initial selection (large base) with progressive screening rather than creating an exclusive elect; maintain open opportunity and successive selection stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Territories and Insular Possessions in allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is intended that the proposed scholarships shall be available also to secondary school graduates in the Territories and Insular Possessions ... Allocation of scholarships to the Territories and Insular Possessions, of course, would decrease the State quotas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure program eligibility and quota accounting include U.S. Territories and Insular Possessions when finalizing allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State committee should include secondary-education representative and selection/guidance expert
rubrics_metrics.description: One member of a college or university faculty, trained and experienced in the field of selection and guidance; and one representative of secondary education within the State, usually a secondary school principal or a high school supervisor in the State department of education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State committees must incorporate both higher-education selection expertise and secondary-education perspective to identify and guide talented candidates.
